[Architecture overview](../export-design.html).

## Data extraction {#data-extraction}

The R extraction script receives the selected ObServe trip IDs and extracts each trip in full.

Two source access options are envisaged: a direct database connection or the public ObServe API.

See [Load an ObServe trip](../../source-loading.html) for both extraction paths.

`observe_sql_extract_trip_csv()` writes one CSV per source table from a database connection.

`observe_public_api_extract_trip_csv()` writes the same files from the public API.

Preserve source identifiers and parent links so the later transformation can navigate the trip's records.

Keep trip-selection criteria in point 01; all per-trip extraction operations use the selected trip identifier.

The SQL queries and intermediate model below describe the database extraction path.

Output conventions and failure handling are covered in point 08.

The [PS extraction model](ps-extraction.html) covers the complete data tree rooted at `ps_common.trip`.

## ObServe LL intermediate form model

The model describes ObServe data using its field names, types, identifiers and relationships.

It has no META sheet. ROS-specific metadata is supplied when preparing the ROS output.

The LL model defines 18 source tables, including repeated measurements, gear compositions and associations.

Each sheet is named after its qualified source table, including schema and table name.

| Sheet / source table                       | Parent sheet                |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------------- |
| `ll_common.trip`                           | —                           |
| `ll_observation.activity`                  | `ll_common.trip`            |
| `ll_observation.fishingSet`                | `ll_observation.activity`   |
| `ll_observation.catch`                     | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_common.trip_species`                   | `ll_common.trip`            |
| `ll_common.gearUseFeatures`                | `ll_common.trip`            |
| `ll_common.gearUseFeaturesMeasurement`     | `ll_common.gearUseFeatures` |
| `ll_observation.hooksComposition`          | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_observation.baitsComposition`          | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_observation.floatlinesComposition`     | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_observation.branchlinesComposition`    | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_observation.fishingSet_mitigationType` | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_observation.section`                   | `ll_observation.fishingSet` |
| `ll_observation.basket`                    | `ll_observation.section`    |
| `ll_observation.branchline`                | `ll_observation.basket`     |
| `ll_observation.sizeMeasure`               | `ll_observation.catch`      |
| `ll_observation.weightMeasure`             | `ll_observation.catch`      |
| `ll_observation.catch_predator`            | `ll_observation.catch`      |

The model belongs conceptually to `observe.form.model`; its YAML lives in `ros.form.observe`.

The source model and SQL queries are shared by ROS form versions under the same ObServe version and gear.

[Download the ObServe 10.0 LL model](../../10.0/ll/form.yaml).

Source NOT NULL flags define mandatory values within source rows; they do not require an empty table to have rows.

Each added table retains its domain fields. Persistence audit columns and internal list indexes are excluded.

Retain every measurement and composition row with its source key and parent; combine them only during transformation.

The three membership tables retain composite keys. They have no invented `topiaId`.

Optional catch links to section, basket and branchline stay as source fields, alongside its required set parent.

The form schema has one `parent_key` per sheet; it does not enforce those additional catch links.

Source fields retain their ObServe IDs; catalogue lookups use `topiaid`. Countries and species groups supply context.

Equipment values remain text until interpreted through characteristic units, types and allowed list items.

Trip equipment and characteristic measurements are additional source candidates; their ROS use remains unconfirmed.

Their existence does not establish populated tori-line measurements or resolve branchline-section questions.

Tags and photo references remain on catch rows. People, vessels and reference values remain in their catalogues.

META uses user input. Optional V-ATTRIBUTES remains outside ObServe population, pending RAV consolidation.

No established LL mapping requires instrument recordings or encounter sightings; these do not become catch records.

Keep ObServe meanings intact. ROS identifiers, code conversions and reporting calculations belong to transformation.

This source model does not resolve missing observations, sampling protocols or the agreed open reporting questions.

## SQL extraction and CSV files

Use one parameterized query per ObServe sheet. Bind the same selected trip ID to every query for that export.

The 18 PostgreSQL queries live in `inst/10.0/ll/sql/`, named `<schema>.<table>.sql` after their source tables.

Each sheet name is its database table name; append `.sql` to obtain the query filename.

Each query binds `$1::text` to one `ll_common.trip.topiaId`, directly or through its owning parent records.

Date, programme and observation-method filters belong to trip selection; these queries retain the whole selected trip.

Join only owning ancestors. Do not combine independent measurements, compositions or reference records in extraction.

Order entity rows by `topiaId` and association rows by their full composite key. Preserve source nulls and values.

Queries must return exactly the model fields, in declaration order, with their declared names.

The CSV header occupies row 1; data begins on row 2. The model declares `start_row: 2`.

A reader that removes CSV headers must adapt the input before using worksheet-oriented diagnostics.

The extraction contract preserves source identifiers, row meaning and parent relationships.

Verify that contract during SQL development, including checks for duplicated rows and broken relationships.

The normal export pipeline trusts the extraction contract; it has no intermediate diagnostic validation stage.

Both paths use the default `sql/csv` format described in the [trip-loading guide](../../source-loading.html).
